_comment: WHAT EACH AGENT IMAGE MUST AND MUST NOT CONTAIN, as data.
Adapted from containerfiles/stage-contract.json in the sshadowforge forge,
and it exists here for the same reason it exists there: `microdnf' resolves a
dependency CLOSURE. `the build agent cannot reach a registry' is true only
until something drags skopeo in as a transitive dependency of something else,
and nothing would notice. This file turns a property that is currently
structural into an executable assertion, checked against the bytes of a built
image rather than against the intent of a Containerfile.
IT RUNS BEFORE PUBLISH, NOT AFTER. The Nexus OCI repository is ALLOW_ONCE: a
tag that has been pushed can never be rewritten, so an image found bad after
publication has permanently burned its name. Checking at build time costs
The forbidden lists are not symmetric decoration. build/skopeo and
publish/kaniko are the two halves of one split and each names the other.
_floor: Every agent image is entitled to assume these and every rootfs script uses
them. The Azure Pipelines agent itself needs bash, tar, gzip and curl to
unpack and update tasks; git is on the floor because a pipeline that cannot
check out its own sources is not an agent.
_images: required  -- the tools this image exists to run, beyond the floor.
forbidden -- what its capability boundary says it must not be able to do.
`entrypoint' is asserted too. All agent images entrypoint on start-agent.sh:
an image that registered with Azure DevOps by some other path would not
deregister on exit, and dead agents accumulate in the pool until the next

azdo-agent-build.note: Runs repository-supplied pipeline YAML. Holds NO registry credential and carries no client that could use one. kaniko is invoked with --no-push unconditionally; the flag is discipline, the absent skopeo is the device.

azdo-agent-publish.note: Holds the Nexus OCI OAuth2 client. CANNOT AUTHOR WHAT IT MOVES -- no kaniko, no envbuilder, no compiler. Carries `registry' only to re-serve the filesystem layout envbuilder wrote, on 127.0.0.1, for the length of one skopeo copy; see docs/envbuilder-output.md. Carries no cosign: signing is the other half of the split and is phase 2.

_scripts: The rootfs scripts are checked as SOURCE on every image, not just where they
run. `scripts_must_not_invoke' is the stronger of the two assertions in this
file: it fails on the line that would have broken rather than on the image
The build scripts must never NAME a push flag. kaniko is perfectly capable of
pushing -- that is what --destination is for -- and the build agent must never
_script_assertions: Per-script, because the two builders fail in opposite directions.
kaniko-build.sh: --no-push must be present and must be UNPARAMETERISABLE.
Note that --destination is NOT forbidden and must not be: kaniko needs a name
for the image it assembles even when it is not pushing it, and the forge
passes both (golden/scripts/image.sh). Forbidding --destination would forbid a
flag kaniko requires. What matters is that --no-push is a literal, so no
environment variable a pipeline controls can turn the push back on.
envbuilder-build.sh is the inverse and the reason is worth writing down.
envbuilder has no --no-push: producing a distributable image REQUIRES
ENVBUILDER_PUSH_IMAGE=true plus a cache repo. Setting
ENVBUILDER_LAYER_CACHE_DIR makes envbuilder start its own in-process registry
over that directory and OVERRIDE the cache repo with it (envbuilder.go:384-394,
`Overriding cache repo with local registry...'), so the push is to 127.0.0.1
and needs no credential. The assertion is therefore not `never push' but
`never name a remote cache repo, and always set the layer cache dir that
redirects the push to loopback'. See docs/envbuilder-output.md.
THE PATTERNS ARE REGEXES, NOT SUBSTRINGS, and that was found by running
scripts/selftest-linters.sh. `--no-push' as a plain substring is satisfied by
`--no-push-cache', which appears two lines below it -- so deleting the real
--no-push flag left the assertion passing. The lookahead is what makes it an
assertion about a FLAG rather than about a sequence of characters.

_why: The first version of this assertion forbade ENVBUILDER_CACHE_REPO
outright, on the reading that ENVBUILDER_LAYER_CACHE_DIR alone redirects
the push to loopback. It does -- but envbuilder rejects an empty cache
repo at line 141, BEFORE it applies that override at line 386, so the
variable has to be set. The assertion is therefore not `never name a
cache repo' but `never name one that is not loopback': what matters is
that the push cannot reach a real registry, not that a variable is unset.
kaniko derives its working directory from proc/self/exe and adds that
DIRECTORY to its ignore list. An executor staged at the chroot root
makes the ignored directory `/', so kaniko ignores the entire
filesystem: the build succeeds, reports a digest, and every layer is
EMPTY. Nothing else in this repository would catch that -- the image
is well-formed, just void. Staging under /kaniko/ is the fix, and this
assertion is what stops it drifting back.
